proposed_statements.scope: Arbitrary finite binary matrices for the extension lemma; actual exact-Gram triangle factors for its corollary. No equality of matchings, prescribed permutation, automorphism premise, quadratic residual completion or target existence asserted.
proposed_statements.statement: Over GF(2), for F,H of the same shape an alternating D with FD=H exists exactly when ker(F^T) is contained in ker(H^T) and FH^T is alternating. Such a D can additionally satisfy D1=0 exactly when H1=0 and every x with F^T x=1 has H^T x=0. For even-n triangle incidence factors with the stated cubic three-cell scaffold and exact integer Gram identity, FH^T=G(I+C) is automatically alternating for H=(I+C)F, so symmetry and zero diagonal add no linear obstruction beyond the known kernel criterion.

proposed_statements.scope: The lower bound is general. No universal rank(B)>=18 claim, no all-core census, and no real/binary rank identification. The two annealer matrices are nonfactor diagnostics only.
proposed_statements.statement: Any symmetric block completion A=[[B,E],[E^T,D]] has rank(A)>=2 rank([B,E])-rank(B). In an even-n triangle scaffold with two incidences per cell in each outside column, three explicit common kernel vectors imply rank([B,E])<=3n. Thus rank(B)>=18 makes this necessary rank54 test vacuous for n12; the five frozen admissible cores satisfy this sufficient condition.
